findings.conclusion: Not all registration cancellations emit the retained access-control error; request initiation order matters. This is not successful-registration proof.

proposedFixDirection.provenMinimalNeed: Avoid initiating new native PWA operations from a departing document. The registration cell establishes beforeunload is earlier than the failing operation, whereas pagehide is later.
lifecycleRequirements: Establish lifetime observation before delayed PwaStatus/startPwa work; a listener added only after beforeunload has already fired cannot fence late startup.
Invalidate registration generation and detach callbacks at departure; check the lifetime before each native operation across awaited cache stages, not only after hasOfflineApp resolves.
Preserve BFCache restoration with pageshow ownership and handle canceled navigation safely; do not leave a still-visible document permanently disabled.
Do not filter native errors, catch unrelated global errors, disable service workers, alter acceptance budgets, or replace original promises for diagnosis.

If cache error is independently bound to page-side readiness reads, consider worker-owned readiness via bounded MessageChannel/event.waitUntil; current evidence does not justify claiming that mechanism is already proven.
requiredValidation: Meaningful lifecycle units: late startup after departure, registration settlement after departure, cache await between stages, duplicate cleanup, BFCache return and canceled-navigation recovery.
Deterministic controlled browser regression that tests production lifecycle ownership at the held replacement boundary, retains unfiltered pageerrors and proves native operation not entered.
Original static-deployment matrix with unchanged deadlines/errors assertion, preserved historical failures and new explicit receipts.

limitations: ENTER-only wrappers and lifecycle logging change scheduling; zero errors in one frozen-app cell does not prove absence of the historical race.
Control and held cells deliberately call native APIs from a synthetic fixture, so this is engine-mechanism reproduction, not source13 application-callback attribution.
No raw traces, request headers, credentials, cache payloads, cookies or private user data were recorded.
